sections.description:
Short title extent and commencement

ORDINANCE, LXXVII OF 1994
ORDINANCE, LXXVII OF 1994
TELECOMMUNICATIONS ORDINANCE, 1994
1. Short title, extent and commencement.‑‑(1) This
Ordinance may be called the Telecommunications Ordinance, 1994. (2) It extends
to the whole of Pakistan,
(3) It shall come into force at
once.

Definitions

ORDINANCE, LXXVII OF 1994
ORDINANCE, LXXVII OF 1994
TELECOMMUNICATIONS ORDINANCE, 1994
2. Definitions: ‑In this Ordinance, unless there is anything
repugnant in the subject or context,‑‑
(a) "Authority" means
the Pakistan Telecommunication Authority established under section 3;
(b) "basic telephone
services" means the provision of domestic or international
telecommunication services for transmission over the public switched network of
two‑way live voice telephone service but shall not include the provision
of any terminal equipment at customer's premises; and
(c) "Board" means
Frequency Allocation Board established under section 19; .
(d) "Company" means
the Pakistan Telecommunication Company Limited established and incorporated in
accordance with section 11;
(e) "competitive
services" means the telecommunication services that may be provided by two
or more licensees;
(f) "Corporation"
means the Pakistan Telecommunications Corporation established under the
Pakistan Telecommunication Corporation Act, 1991 (XVIII of 1991);
(g) "domestic
telecommunication services" means the telecommunication services provided
within Pakistan;
(h) "international
telecommunication services" means the telecommunication services provided
between Pakistan and any other country;
(i) "licence" means
an authorisation granted by the Authority for the provision of domestic or
international telecommunication services;
(j) "licensee" means
holder of a licence;
(k) "member" means a
member of the Authority;
(1) "person" mans any
individual, partnership, association, joint stock company, joint venture, trust
or corporation;
(m) "prescribed"
means prescribed by rules made under this Ordinance;
(n) "public switched
network" means the telecommunication network, consisting of a fully
interconnected and integrated system of various means of transmission and
switching utilized to provide basic telephone service and other
telecommunication services to the general public;
(o) "telecommunication
services" means any domestic or international transmission, emission or
reception of signs, signals, writings, pictures, sounds or information of any
nature by wire, radio, electricity, optical media or other electro‑magnetic
system; and
(p) "transfer date" means the date
appointed by the Federal Government for transfer of assets and liabilities of
the Corporation to the Company in accordance with section 11.

Establishment of the telecommunications authority

ORDINANCE, LXXVII OF 1994
ORDINANCE, LXXVII OF 1994
TELECOMMUNICATIONS ORDINANCE, 1994
3. Establishment
of Pakistan Telecommunications Authority.‑‑(l) As soon as may
be after the commencement of this Ordinance, the Federal Government shall
establish the Pakistan Telecommunication Authority consisting of three Members
one of whom shall be a professional telecommunication engineer and one other
shall be a financial expert.
(2) Every member shall be appointed by the Federal
Government for a term of four years and shall be eligible for re‑appointment
for a similar or a shorter term or terms.
(3) The Federal Government shall from amongst the
members appointed under subsection (2) appoint a member as Chairman of the
Authority;
(4) The decision of the Authority shall be taken with
the concurrence of the majority of its members.
(5) A member shall not have any direct or indirect
financial interest in, or have connection with, any establishment or a firm
which renders telecommunication services in Pakistan or supplies equipments to
any telecommunication sector.
Explanation.‑‑For
the purpose of this subsection, any involvement of the spouse or any blood
relation of any member with any telecommunication establishment or firm shall
be considered as a direct financial interest or connection of the member with
such establishment or firm.
(6) A member may resign from his office by writing in
his hand or may be removed from his office if, on an inquiry by the Federal
Public Service Commission, he is found unable to perform the functions of his
office because of mental or physical disability or misconduct.
(7) In case of death, resignation or removal of a
member, another person may be appointed for the unexpired term of such member.
(8) Every member shall be paid honoraria equivalent
to the salary and perquisites admissible annually to a Judge of the High Court
or such higher emoluments as the Federal Government may determine.
(9) No act or proceeding of the
Authority shall be invalid by reason only of the existence of a vacancy in, or
a defect in, constitution of the Authority.

Objects of the authority

ORDINANCE, LXXVII OF 1994
ORDINANCE, LXXVII OF 1994
TELECOMMUNICATIONS ORDINANCE, 1994
4. Objects of the Authority.‑‑The
objects of the Authority shall be to‑‑
(a) promote the availability of
a wide range of high quality, efficient and cost effective telecommunication
services throughout the country;
(b) promote technological
innovation and rapid modernization of public switched network;
(c) plan and regulate the
commercial use of the radio frequency spectrum to achieve efficiency, economy,
utility and orderly growth of competitive in telecommunication services;
(d) provide for the
privatization of the Pakistan Telecommunications Corporation on such terms and
conditions as the Federal Government may deem fit; and
(e) safeguard national
security.

Powers and functions of the authority

ORDINANCE, LXXVII OF 1994
ORDINANCE, LXXVII OF 1994
TELECOMMUNICATIONS ORDINANCE, 1994
5. Powers and functions of the Authority.‑‑(I) The
Authority shall be responsible for regulating the provision of
telecommunication services in Pakistan and grant of licences to private and public
telecommunication operators.
(2) In particular, and without
prejudice to the generality of the foregoing, the Authority shall‑‑‑
(i) grant and renew licences
for telecommunication services in accordance with the policies and guidelines
set out by the Federal Government;
(ii) administer the radio
frequency spectrum allocated to telecommunication services by the Board;
(iii) specify standards for locally manufactured
telecommunication equipments and determine compatibility and standards of
imported telecommunication equipments;
(iv) monitor compliance of conditions of the licences
issued to the Company and other licensees;
(v) advise the Federal Government for adopting
policies and guidelines for the regulation of telecommunication services;
(vi) review inter‑connection
contracts;
(vii) provide protection against anti‑competitive
conduct of the licensees;
(viii) regulate tariffs of the
Company and other licensees;
(ix) resolve complaints and
other claims against licensees for contravention of the provisions of this
Ordinance;
(x) determine and collect fees
and charges levied under this Ordinance;
(xi) make recommendations to
the Federal Government on policies with respect to international
telecommunications, provision of support for the Federal Government's
participation in international meetings and agreements to be executed in
relation to the routing of international traffic and accounting settlements;
(xii) appoint, promote, remove and exercise
discipline and control over its staff;
(xiii) set up its internal
organizations, including bureaus, divisions or offices and make appointments of
the heads of such bureaus, divisions and offices; and
(xiv) enter into contracts.
(3) Any request for review of any decision or order
of Authority shall be addressed directly to the Authority in the form of a
request for reconsideration.
(4) Any person aggrieved of the
decision of the Authority made under subsection (1) or subsection (3) may,
within sixty days of the receipt of such decision or order, prefer an appeal to
the High Court.
(S) The Authority shall act as Vigilance Commission
with respect to complaints made by the public in relation to telecommunication
services and carry out inspections of telegraphs and telephones for monitoring
and implementation of technical conditions and requirements.

Staff and advisors

ORDINANCE, LXXVII OF 1994
ORDINANCE, LXXVII OF 1994
TELECOMMUNICATIONS ORDINANCE, 1994
6. Staff and
Advisors.‑‑(1) The officers and staff of the Authority, other
than its members, shall be civil servants within the meaning of the .Civil
Servants Act, 1973 (LXXI of 1973).
(2) The Authority may appoint consultants and
advisors on contract to carry out purposes of this Act on such terms and
conditions as it may determine.

Advisory committees

ORDINANCE, LXXVII OF 1994
ORDINANCE, LXXVII OF 1994
TELECOMMUNICATIONS ORDINANCE, 1994
7. Advisory Committees.‑‑The Authority
may, whenever it thinks fit, appoint advisory committees consisting of such
persons .having appropriate expertise to represent the views and interests of
users and operators and to advise the members and their staff on policy and
technical matters.

Funds of the authority

ORDINANCE, LXXVII OF 1994
ORDINANCE, LXXVII OF 1994
TELECOMMUNICATIONS ORDINANCE, 1994
8. Funds of
the Authority.‑‑(l) The operations of the Authority shall be
funded from the following sources namely:‑‑
(i) grants from the Federal Government and Provincial
Governments, including initial grant of fifty million rupees by the Federal
Government.
(ii) loans raised by the
Authority;
(iii) prescribed .fees for processing of various
applications made under this Act and annual fees payable by the licensees; and
(iv) annual fee payable by the licensees to the
Authority, not exceeding 0.33% of the annual gross revenue of each licensee.
(2) The Funds of the Authority shall be administered
through accounts to be maintained with the nationalised banks.

Budget of the authority

ORDINANCE, LXXVII OF 1994
ORDINANCE, LXXVII OF 1994
TELECOMMUNICATIONS ORDINANCE, 1994
9. Budget of
the Authority.‑‑(l) The Authority shall, by or before the first
day of June every year, submit for approval to the Federal Government a budget
for its operations during the next financial year.
(2) Any surplus of fees recovered over the approved
amount specified in the budget in a year shall be remitted to the Federal
Consolidated Fund and any deficit from fees than the estimated amount shown in
the annual budget shall be made up by the Federal Government through
appropriations.

Reports

ORDINANCE, LXXVII OF 1994
ORDINANCE, LXXVII OF 1994
TELECOMMUNICATIONS ORDINANCE, 1994
10. Reports.‑‑The
Authority shall submit an annual report of its operations and activities to,
and such other reports as may be required by the Federal Government.

Establishment of the company

ORDINANCE, LXXVII OF 1994
ORDINANCE, LXXVII OF 1994
TELECOMMUNICATIONS ORDINANCE, 1994
11. Establishment of the
Company.‑‑(1) As soon as may be after the commencement of this
Ordinance, the Federal Government shall establish a company to be known as the
Pakistan Telecommunication Company, limited by shares, and cause it to be
incorporated under the Companies Ordinance, 1984 (XLVII of 1984), with the
principal object of provision of domestic and international telecommunication
and related services consistent with the provisions of this Ordinance.
(2) The Federal Government
shall nominate seven persons to .subscribe to the Memorandum and Articles of
Association of the Company.
(3) Initially, all shares of
the Company shall be issued to, or held in trust for, the President.
(4) As from the transfer date,
such assets and liabilities of the Corporation shall, as the Federal Government
may determine by a notification in the official Gazette, stand transferred to
the Company:
Provided that the Federal
Government may itself retain such number of shares in the Company as it may
determine.
(5) The Federal Government
shall, immediately on incorporation of the Company fix a date by a notice in
the official Gazette for election of the Board of Directors of the Company
consisting of seven directors in accordance with the provisions of the
Companies Ordinance, 1984 (XLVII of 1984):
Provided that, notwithstanding
the election of the Board of Directors of the Company, the Board of Directors
appointed under section 4 of the Pakistan Telecommunication Corporation Act,
1991 (XVIII of 1991), shall continue to function till such time as the Federal
Government may decide for the finalization of accounts of the Corporation and
completion of transfer process of the assets and liabilities of the Corporation
referred to in subsection (5) to the Company.

Transfer of employees of the corporation

ORDINANCE, LXXVII OF 1994
ORDINANCE, LXXVII OF 1994
TELECOMMUNICATIONS ORDINANCE, 1994
12. Transfer of employees of
the Corporation.‑‑(1) Notwithstanding anything contained in any law
for the time being in force, as from the transfer date, all employees of the
Corporation, whether recruited initially or became such employees under section
9 of the Pakistan Telecommunication Corporation Act, 1991 (XVIII of 1991),
shall stand transferred to, and become employees of the Company on the same
terms and conditions which were applicable to them immediately prior to the
transfer date and thereby cease to be the employees of the Corporation:
Provided that after the
transfer date, such employees shall no longer be deemed to be public servants
within the meaning of section 21 of the Pakistan Penal Code (Act XLV of 1860).
(2) The Company shall be
empowered to make appointment of such additional employees and consultants as
it deems necessary to achieve its objects and to carry out its business.

Special provisions

ORDINANCE, LXXVII OF 1994
ORDINANCE, LXXVII OF 1994
TELECOMMUNICATIONS ORDINANCE, 1994
13. Special provisions.‑‑Notwithstanding
anything contained in the Companies Ordinance, 1984 (XLVII of 1984),‑‑
(a) that till such time the
Federal Government may determine, different classes of shares may have
different voting rights relating to the responsibilities for the management and
corporate governance of the Company; and
(b) that the provisions of subsection (1) of section 206 of
the said Ordinance shall not apply to any agreement or contract approved by the
Federal Government in relation to the Comp

Licence to the company

ORDINANCE, LXXVII OF 1994
ORDINANCE, LXXVII OF 1994
TELECOMMUNICATIONS ORDINANCE, 1994
14. Licence to the company.‑‑(1) The Authority shall grant a licence to the Company for the
provision of basic telephone services for a period of twenty five years
renewable within two years before the expiry of the initial term at the
discretion of the Federal Government for such period or periods as it may deem
appropriate.
(2) The Company shall, under
the licence, have the exclusive right to provide basic telephone services in
Pakistan, excluding the Northern Areas and Azad Jammu and Kashmir, for a period
of seven years.
(3) Notwithstanding the
exclusive rights of the Company referred in subsection (2), the Authority may,
in accordance with the policy laid down by the Federal Government and any
condition specified in the licence, permit mobile telephone services, including
cellular radio mobile telephones, paging and personal telecommunication
services on competitive basis.

National telecommunication corporation

ORDINANCE, LXXVII OF 1994
ORDINANCE, LXXVII OF 1994
TELECOMMUNICATIONS ORDINANCE, 1994
15. National Telecommunication
Corporation.‑‑Notwithstanding anything contained hereinbefore or the Pakistan Telecommunication Corporation
Act, 1991 (XVIII of 1991), the Federal
Government may establish a National Telecommunication Corporation for provision
of telecommunication services to armed forces, defence projects, Federal
Government, Provincial Governments, Local
authorities or such other agencies or institutions as the Federal Government
may determine.

Competitive services licencees

ORDINANCE, LXXVII OF 1994
ORDINANCE, LXXVII OF 1994
TELECOMMUNICATIONS ORDINANCE, 1994
16. Competitive services
licensees: ‑‑(l) Without prejudice to subsection (2) of section 14,
in order to ensure the provision of telecommunication services on competitive
basis and in pursuance of objectives of this Ordinance, the Authority may, with
the approval of the Federal Government,
in addition to the Company, grant licence to any person or class of persons
subject to qualifications and conditions as may be prescribed.
(2) Any person providing
telecommunication services immediately before
the transfer date shall be deemed to be a licensee under this Ordinance:
Provided that the licence or
contract under which such services are provided
shall be subject to such terms and conditions as may be laid down by the Authority under this Ordinance and the
rules and regulations made ` thereunder.

Unlicensed services

ORDINANCE, LXXVII OF 1994
ORDINANCE, LXXVII OF 1994
TELECOMMUNICATIONS ORDINANCE, 1994
17. Unlicensed services: ‑‑The
Federal Government may, on the advice of the
Authority, allow certain services or operations of telecommunications without a
licence.

Transfer of assignment of licences

ORDINANCE, LXXVII OF 1994
ORDINANCE, LXXVII OF 1994
TELECOMMUNICATIONS ORDINANCE, 1994
18. Transfer of assignment of
licences.‑‑No licence shall, without the prior approval of the
Authority, be liable to assignment or transfer:
Provided that no person or
establishment shall, without the prior approval
of the Federal Government, be allowed to acquire directly or indirectly ten per
cent or more of the shares of the Company.

Frequency allocation board

ORDINANCE, LXXVII OF 1994
ORDINANCE, LXXVII OF 1994
TELECOMMUNICATIONS ORDINANCE, 1994
19. Frequency Allocation Board:
‑‑(1) The Federal Government shall, by a notification in the official Gazette establish a Frequency
Allocation Board to take over the
functions performed by the Pakistan Wireless Board which shall, from the date
of such notification. stand dissolved.

Powers and functions of the board

ORDINANCE, LXXVII OF 1994
ORDINANCE, LXXVII OF 1994
TELECOMMUNICATIONS ORDINANCE, 1994
20. Powers and functions of the Board.‑‑(1)
The Board shall, have exclusive authority to allocate portions of the radio
frequency spectrum to commercial telecommunication services, radio and
television broadcasting operations, Government, public and private wireless
operators.
(2) The Board shall consist of‑‑‑
(i) Secretary, Ministry of
Communications. Chairman:
(ii) Executive Director of the
Board. Vice‑Chairman:
(iii) the Chairman of the
Authority. Member:
and
(iv) a nominee each of the
Ministry
of Defence (Corps of Signals),
Ministry of Information and
Broad‑'
casting and Ministry of
Interior. Members
(3) The Vice‑Chairman shall devote full time to
the business of the Board and shall not hold any other office or position
during his service as such Vice‑Chairman and shall be responsible for
good administration of the Board.
(4) In exercise of its powers under subsection (1),
the Board shall be guided by the applicable recommendations of the
International Telecommunications Union or any of its standing committees or
organizations, including the International Consultative Committee on
Telecommunications the International Consultative Committee on Radio, the
International Frequency Registration Board and other concerned international
organizations.
(5) Every application for allocation of radio
frequency spectrum to telecommunication services and radio and television
broadcasting operations to the Pakistan Broadcasting Corporation and to other
Governmental or private agencies shall be made to the Board through the
Authority. .
(6) The Authority shall, on receipt of an application
made under subsection (5) and after necessary classification of
telecommunication services and operations, move to the Board for its approval
for such services and operations and after such approval, the Authority shall
assign specific frequencies within a service to particular users.

Responsibilities of the federal Government

ORDINANCE, LXXVII OF 1994
ORDINANCE, LXXVII OF 1994
TELECOMMUNICATIONS ORDINANCE, 1994
21. Responsibilities of the Federal Government.‑‑The
Federal Government shall‑‑
(a) lay down policies and guidelines for the
regulation of telecommunication services;
(b) specify criteria for the grant and renewal of
licences by the Authority;
(c) specify the scale of fees
of licences and for renewal thereof;
(d) call reports from time to
time about the activities of the Authority and
Board; and
(e) provide for representation
in meetings of the international telecommunication
organizations.

Accounting procedures

ORDINANCE, LXXVII OF 1994
ORDINANCE, LXXVII OF 1994
TELECOMMUNICATIONS ORDINANCE, 1994
22. Accounting procedures: ‑‑(1)
The Authority shall prescribe accounting
procedures for the costs of operations which shall be adopted by the Company
and other licensees.
(2) The costs of all basic
telecommunication services provided by any licensee shall be accounted for
separately from the costs of any competitive services provided by the licensee.

Tariffs

ORDINANCE, LXXVII OF 1994
ORDINANCE, LXXVII OF 1994
TELECOMMUNICATIONS ORDINANCE, 1994
23. Tariffs: ‑‑(1) The tariffs for telecommunication
services shall‑‑
(i) be based on price and cost
of service requirements as may be prescribed;
(ii) not be unreasonably
discriminatory; and
(iii) be compatible with, and
promote the development of, competitive services as determined by the Authority
from time to time.
(2) Except in the case of the
Company, the tariffs to be levied by the Authority shall be subject to the
terms and conditions of the licence and contain all information concerning rate
and charges for services, security deposits, non‑recurring charges and
monthly charges and such other terms and conditions as may be prescribed,
including rights and remedies available to customers in the event of
unauthorised charges or other disputes or claims of over‑billing or the
provision of services.

Enforcement of conditions of licence

ORDINANCE, LXXVII OF 1994
ORDINANCE, LXXVII OF 1994
TELECOMMUNICATIONS ORDINANCE, 1994
24. Enforcement of conditions
of licence.‑‑(l) Subject to concurrence of the Authority and the
licensee, the Authority may without the approval of the Federal Governments
amend any licence in conformity with the provisions of this Ordinance.
(2) Where the Authority in
pursuance of the provision of this Ordinance, desires to amend any licence and
the licensee does not agree to such amendment, the Authority may, with the
approval of the Federal Government, amend such licence:
Provided that the licence for
basic telephone services of the Company shall not, except with its consent, be
amended during the period of its exclusive rights.

Issue of enforcement order

ORDINANCE, LXXVII OF 1994
ORDINANCE, LXXVII OF 1994
TELECOMMUNICATIONS ORDINANCE, 1994
25. Issue of enforcement order: ‑‑If any
licensee contravenes the terms and conditions of the licence the Authority may
issue an enforcement order requiring the licensee to‑‑
(i) comply with such order; or
(ii) agree on a course of
action with the Authority to remedy the contravention, within thirty days of
the said order.

Penalty of contravention of terms of licences

ORDINANCE, LXXVII OF 1994
ORDINANCE, LXXVII OF 1994
TELECOMMUNICATIONS ORDINANCE, 1994
26. Penalty
for contravention of terms of licences.‑‑(l) Where a licensee fails
either to comply with, or contravenes any condition of the licence even after
issue of enforcement order under section 25 or fails to pay the licence fee
within the specified period the Authority may‑‑
(a) levy financial penalties
against the licensee; and
(b) depending upon the severity
of the offence suspend, revoke or terminate a licence with the prior approval
of the Federal Government.
(2) Notwithstanding anything
contained in subsection (1) the Authority may, with the prior approval of the
Federal Government, suspend, revoke or terminate a licence where the licensee
dies or the licensee's establishment is wound up.
(3) In addition to any other
penalty that may be imposed under this Ordinance or any other law for the time
being in force, any person operating a telecommunication service without a
licence under this Ordinance shall be punishable with fine which may extend to
ten million rupees.
(4) Where a person‑‑‑
(a) makes abusive, threatening or obscene calls; or
(b) uses a telecommunication
service knowing it to be without a licence; or
(c) contravenes any order
enforcing a licence or rules or regulations made under this Ordinance; or
(d) engages in interception of,
or tracing of, telecommunication operations or messages unless authorised by
the sender, recipient, the Authority or any Governmental agency;
he shall be punishable with imprisonment of either
description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may
extend to twenty‑five thousand rupees. or with both.
(4) No Court shall take
cognizance of any offence punishable under this Ordinance except on a complaint
in writing by the Authority.

sections.description:
Technical standards etc

ORDINANCE, LXXVII OF 1994
ORDINANCE, LXXVII OF 1994
TELECOMMUNICATIONS ORDINANCE, 1994
27. Technical standards, etc: ‑‑(1)
The Authority shall supervise the technical standards of telecommunication
equipments, including computers, attached to the public switched network of the
Company and other networks;
Provided that the Authority may
specify different standards for different classes of equipment and may
establish procedures for the testing of the telecommunication apparatuses.
(2) In determining the
standards referred to in subsection (1), the Authority shall ensure that the
standards of equipments are maintained to ensure a safe and efficient
telecommunications environment.
(3) All licensees shall comply
with the technical standards established by the Authority with respect to
operational compatibility, minimum service quality and inter‑connection
of networks.

National security

ORDINANCE, LXXVII OF 1994
ORDINANCE, LXXVII OF 1994
TELECOMMUNICATIONS ORDINANCE, 1994
28. National Security.‑‑(I)
Notwithstanding anything contained in any law for the time being in force, in
the interest of national security or in the apprehension of any offence, the
Federal Government may authorise any person or persons to intercept calls and
messages or to trace calls through the telecommunications network. .
(2) During a war or hostilities
against Pakistan by any foreign power or internal aggression or for the defence
or security of Pakistan, the Federal Government shall have preference and
priority in telecommunication networks over any licensee.
(3) Upon proclamation of
emergency by the President, the Federal Government may suspend or modify all or
any orders or licences made or issued under this Ordinance or cause suspension
of operation, functions or services of any licence or company for such time as
it may deem necessary:
Provided that the Federal
Government may compensate any licensee whose facilities or services are
affected by any action under this subsection.

Acquisition of land for the company

ORDINANCE, LXXVII OF 1994
ORDINANCE, LXXVII OF 1994
TELECOMMUNICATIONS ORDINANCE, 1994
29. Acquisition of land for the
Company: ‑‑Any acquisition of land made by the Government on behalf
of the Company shall be deemed an acquisition for public purposes under the
Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (I of 1894), and the provisions of the said Act
shall, mutatis mutandis, apply to such acquisition.

Transfer of shares of the company

ORDINANCE, LXXVII OF 1994
ORDINANCE, LXXVII OF 1994
TELECOMMUNICATIONS ORDINANCE, 1994
30. Transfer
of shares of the Company: ‑‑(1) The Federal Government may,
whenever deem appropriate, transfer the shares of the Company to private
investors or the general public on such terms and conditions and manner as it
may determine through competitive bids, private placement or public offers.

Tax holidays

ORDINANCE, LXXVII OF 1994
ORDINANCE, LXXVII OF 1994
TELECOMMUNICATIONS ORDINANCE, 1994
31. Tax Holidays.‑‑‑The Company shall, subject to
approval by the Federal Government, not be liable to pay any income tax, super
tax or wealth tax on its income, profits or gains for a period of three years
from the transfer date.

Rules and regulations

ORDINANCE, LXXVII OF 1994
ORDINANCE, LXXVII OF 1994
TELECOMMUNICATIONS ORDINANCE, 1994
32. Rules and regulations: ‑‑(1) The
Federal Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, make rules to
regulate the functions of .the Board, including procedure for the submission of
applications and action thereon.
(2) The Board may, with the prior approval of the
Federal Government, make regulations to carry out its purposes under this
Ordinance, including laying down the scales of licence fees.
(3) The Authority may, with the approval of the
Federal Government, make bye‑laws for carrying out its day to day
functions.

Ordinance to override certain laws

ORDINANCE, LXXVII OF 1994
ORDINANCE, LXXVII OF 1994
TELECOMMUNICATIONS ORDINANCE, 1994
33. Ordinance to override certain laws: ‑‑The
provisions of this Ordinance shall have effect notwithstanding anything
contained in the Wireless Telegraphy Act, 1933 (XVII of 1933), or any other law
containing any provision inconsistent to this Ordinance.

Repeal

ORDINANCE, LXXVII OF 1994
ORDINANCE, LXXVII OF 1994
TELECOMMUNICATIONS ORDINANCE, 1994
34. Repeal: ‑‑The Telecommunications
Ordinance, 1994 (LI of 1994) is hereby repealed
